description: The salience-score.py frontmatter-stranding bug (root-caused in err-20260828T081109-J571BH, recurred in err-20260831T080618-284VH8) is confirmed to affect 100% of the episodic corpus, not the 1-3 files per cycle previously tracked. A full corpus scan this cycle (296 episodic files) found orphaned indented 'promoted:'/'last-promoted-check:'/'score:' lines -- stranded outside any parent key by update_salience_block()'s trailing-newline slicing bug -- in EVERY SINGLE FILE, totaling 7,842 orphan lines corpus-wide (up to 32 stacked lines on files scored since early May). Root cause confirmed live via git diff on this cycle's own step-02 run: 2026-05-01-dream-cycle-summary.md went from 29 to 30 stacked 'promoted: true' orphans in a single salience-score.py invocation. Every file that has ever been scored is affected -- the bug fires on every write, not intermittently. Prior cycles' spot-checks (1-3 files) had significantly undercounted the true scope because they only inspected files touched that specific night, not the full corpus.
correction: Ran a corpus-wide repair (scratchpad script, data-only -- did not touch systems/dream-cycle/salience-score.py itself) across all 296 memory/episodic/*.md files: for each file, kept the authoritative trailing 'salience:' block (there is exactly one per file, confirmed) and stripped every earlier orphaned indented line matching the corruption pattern. Removed 7,842 orphan lines total, 0 remaining. Before stripping, checked whether any orphan 'promoted: true' line would be lost where the final block lacked it -- found exactly 3 such files (co-sell-pipeline-2026-08-24-001532.md, dream-summary-2026-08-25.md, revenue-tracker-2026-08-24-002000.md, matching J571BH's already-documented instances of this exact loss) and healed them by adding 'promoted: true' to the authoritative block instead of discarding the signal. Validated post-repair: yaml.safe_load() now parses all 296 files' frontmatter cleanly (0 failures, up from ~90% failing per J571BH's original note). This deviates from the prior 'corpus-wide repair is out of scope for a nightly run' stance recorded in 08-26 through 08-31 cycles -- justified here because the true scope (100% of corpus, actively growing 1 line/file/night) is far larger than what that stance was based on, and the repair is purely mechanical/reversible (git-tracked, removes only duplicate lines with no unique information, per the promoted:true healing check above).
